evidence: IT Services are 64% of the forecast revenue (INR 41.8 million over the next 26 weeks) and its forecast changes by -7% in units against the same weeks a year earlier (465 against 498). After June 1 the demand was 19% below the forecast of the model that did not know about the slowdown, and the weekly ranges add up to 286 to 599 units.
recommendation: Treat IT Services as the largest revenue risk: find out why demand slowed (pipeline, pricing, renewals), review the forecast every week against the 8-week ratio, and do not cut IT capacity until the ratio stays below -20% for a longer period.
estimated_impact: Scenario: every 10% of IT units is about INR 4.2 million over 26 weeks at INR 89,818 per unit. If IT units ended 10% below even this forecast, that revenue would be lost.

evidence: Digital Services are forecast at 778 units, +45% against the same weeks a year earlier (538). After June 1 demand was 19% above the forecast of the model that did not know about the lift, and the busiest forecast week is 35 units (up to 47 in the range).
recommendation: Plan delivery capacity for Digital Services from the corrected forecast and keep a reserve for the upper end of the range in the busiest weeks; re-check the level every month, since the lift can fade or continue.
estimated_impact: Scenario: planning from last year's 538 units instead of the forecast 778 would leave 240 units without capacity, about INR 2.9 million of revenue at INR 11,993 per unit.

evidence: The 8-week actual-against-forecast ratio left the +/-20% band for IT Services at 2026-07-27 (4 weeks after its slowdown began) and for Digital Services at 2026-09-14 (15 weeks after its lift began), and never for Internship Programs or Training Programs. The weekly noise and the 8-week window are the reason for the delay.
recommendation: Run the 8-week ratio every week for every line, retrain the models every month with the newest weeks, and review any line outside the band; keep the forecast with and without the level correction so that the effect of the change can be seen.
estimated_impact: Process improvement, not a forecast of money: a monitor that flags a change in about one to four months is better than finding it at the end of the year, but it cannot flag it at once.

evidence: The forecast depends on the campaign plan: without campaigns the 26-week total would be 3375 units, with the typical load 3632, and with 50% more campaign days 3768. The lift of +50% campaign days over no campaigns differs by line, from +5% in IT Services to +13% in Digital Services. In revenue, the typical campaigns are worth INR 1.4 million in IT Services against INR 0.1 million in Internship Programs, although the campaign effect of IT Services is the least certain (an interval of +2% to +31% for a full campaign week on Day 46).
recommendation: Share the campaign calendar with the forecast owners before every forecast run, and put the extra campaign days where a campaign adds the most revenue per day, not where it adds the most units.
estimated_impact: Scenario: 50% more campaign days than typical add 136 units, which is about INR 1.7 million of revenue at the revenue per unit of each line, before the cost of the campaigns.

evidence: Internship Programs peak at 68 units a week in January (1.3 times the average week of the forecast), and January and February are the busiest months (67 and 63 units per week, against 44 in October). They are 39% of the forecast units but only 2.6% of the revenue.
recommendation: Plan mentors, seats, and intake dates for the peak weeks and keep the cost per intern low outside them; revenue is small, so the peak is a capacity question and not a growth bet.
estimated_impact: Capacity planning scenario: sizing for the average week would leave the peak weeks about 25% short of the demand; sizing for the peak would leave the average week with idle capacity.

evidence: Training Programs are forecast at 979 units (+11% against the same weeks a year earlier), December has -10% units per week against the average week of all lines (the holidays), and the yearly peak of Training Programs is in July, outside the forecast period.
recommendation: Use the quiet weeks of the holiday period for course preparation and for the campaign days that the plan allows, and prepare the July peak early.
estimated_impact: Not quantified: the gain is a smoother workload, and the simulated data has no cost of preparing a course to turn it into money.

evidence: The selected regression has a WAPE of 7.2% on the weekly total but 10% to 23% by line on the test weeks, its 80% ranges contained 76.9% of the test line-weeks, and it has seen only three years of simulated data.
recommendation: Use the forecast for planning about 26 weeks ahead and not beyond, read it with its ranges, and replace the simulated history with the real inquiry history as soon as it is available.
estimated_impact: Risk control: it avoids planning on a point forecast that the data cannot support.
